expected_english: of (feminine); Possessive particle used when the following noun is feminine.
and; Conjunction used to connect words, phrases, or clauses.
was; Past tense masculine singular form of 'to be'.
will (future marker); Future tense auxiliary marker (masculine singular).
staying / remaining / (cont. marker); Form of the verb 'rahna' (to stay) often used as an auxiliary for continuous actions.
that (conjunction); Conjunction used to link a main clause with a subordinate clause.
were (masculine plural); Past tense masculine plural form of 'to be'.
whom / which / whose (oblique); Oblique singular relative pronoun used before postpositions.
staying / remaining / (cont. masc); Masculine singular form of 'rahna', used as an auxiliary for continuous present/past actions.
staying / remaining / (cont. fem); Feminine singular form of 'rahna', used as an auxiliary for continuous present/past actions.
for / for the sake of; Postposition indicating the purpose, recipient, or reason for an action.
until / up to / even; Postposition indicating a limit in time or space, or emphasis.
they (oblique / respect); Oblique form of 'woh' (plural or formal singular) used before postpositions.
happening / becoming / being; Present participle (masculine plural) of the verb 'hona' (to be/become).
others / second / another; Ordinal number for 'second' or a pronoun/adjective meaning 'others'.
(marker / possessor / fem); Suffix/particle used to turn a noun or verb into an adjective or to indicate possession (feminine).
(marker / possessor / plural); Masculine plural or oblique form of the 'wālā' suffix.
(marker / possessor / masc); Masculine singular suffix used to indicate a person associated with a thing or action.
one's own (oblique / plural); Reflexive possessive pronoun referring back to the subject (masculine plural or oblique).
one's own (feminine); Reflexive possessive pronoun referring back to the subject (feminine singular).
one's own (masculine); Reflexive possessive pronoun referring back to the subject (masculine singular).
whom / those / which (plural oblique); Plural oblique relative pronoun used before postpositions to refer to people or things.
then / again / afterwards; Adverb indicating sequence in time or repetition of an action.
who / which (singular oblique); Singular oblique interrogative pronoun used before postpositions.
which ones; Plural interrogative adjective used to ask for a choice among many.
somewhere / anywhere / (lest); Indefinite adverb of place or a conjunction expressing a fear ('lest').
exactly this / same; Emphatic form of 'yeh', indicating the exact person or thing close at hand.
whom / which (acc / dat); Accusative or dative form of the relative pronoun 'jis'.
who (plural relative oblique); Oblique plural form of the relative pronoun 'jo', used as the subject in perfective tenses with 'ne'.
whose / of which; Possessive form of the relative pronoun 'jis'.
whose (plural) / of which; Possessive plural form of the relative pronoun 'jin'.
your (formal) / yours; Possessive form of the respectful pronoun 'āp'.
your (informal) / yours; Possessive form of the second-person plural or informal pronoun 'tum'.
which; Interrogative adjective used to ask for a choice among alternatives.
how / in what way / why; Formal or literary interrogative adverb meaning 'how' or 'in what manner'.
as much as; Relative adjective or adverb indicating an equal quantity or degree.
as many as; Masculine plural or oblique form of 'jitnā'.
so many; Masculine plural or oblique form of 'itnā'.
in front of / opposite; Postposition indicating position directly ahead or on the other side.
for / for the sake of; Postposition indicating purpose or the person for whom an action is done.
below / under / down; Adverb or postposition indicating a lower position or rank.
behind / back / ago; Adverb or postposition indicating a position at the back or a past time.
month; Noun referring to one of the twelve periods into which a year is divided.
occasionally / once in a while; Adverbial phrase indicating that an action happens infrequently.
to stand / to stand up; Compound verb expressing the act of being on one's feet or rising from a sitting position.
to win / to be victorious; Verb expressing the act of being successful in a contest, conflict, or game.
to lose (defeat) / to fail; Verb meaning to be defeated in a contest or to fail to achieve a goal.
to spend (money / time); Compound verb expressing the act of using money to pay for goods/services or consuming time/energy.
to obtain / to get / to achieve; Compound verb expressing the act of acquiring something through effort or naturally.
to use / to utilize; Compound verb expressing the act of putting something to a purpose or service.
to try / to attempt / to strive; Compound verb expressing the act of making an effort to do something.
to help / to assist / to aid; Compound verb expressing the act of providing support or assistance to someone.
to finish / to end / to terminate; Compound verb expressing the act of bringing something to a conclusion or completion.
to decide / to judge / to resolve; Compound verb expressing the act of making a choice or settling a dispute.
to remember / to memorize / to miss (someone); Compound verb expressing the act of calling back to mind or learning by heart.
to love / to fondle; Compound verb expressing affection or deep emotional attachment to someone.
to smile; Verb meaning to form one's features into a pleased or kind expression.
to jump / to leap; Verb expressing a sudden movement off the ground using legs.
to stop / to stay / to halt; Verb expressing the cessation of motion or an activity.
to imagine / to think / to care; Compound verb meaning to form a mental image, to hold an opinion, or to take care of someone/something.
to be known / to find out / to seem; Compound verb indicating that information has become clear or how something appears to be.
to explain / to make someone understand / to counsel; Causative verb used to clarify a point or to give advice/guidance to someone.
to feed / to make someone play; Causative verb meaning to give food to someone or to facilitate play/entertainment.
to give a drink / to water; Causative verb meaning to make someone drink a liquid or to water plants/animals.
to put to sleep; Causative verb meaning to cause someone (usually a child) to go to sleep.
to cause to be sent; Double causative verb meaning to arrange for someone to send something to another place.
to show / to exhibit / to manifest; Emphatic form of 'dikhānā', used to mean showing something clearly or making it manifest.
to request / to state / to submit (humble); Humble compound verb used by the speaker to refer to their own speaking/requesting to a superior.
to request / to submit / to petition; Formal compound verb used to make a polite request or submission, especially in writing.
to apply / to request / to petition; Compound verb used for making an official application or a formal request.
to order / to command / to decree; Compound verb used by an authority to give a command or instruction.
to promise / to pledge; Compound verb expressing the act of giving a word or assurance that something will be done.
to choose / to select / to elect; Compound verb used for making a selection or voting for a representative.
to travel / to journey; Compound verb expressing the act of going from one place to another over a distance.
to board / to ride / to mount; Compound verb meaning to get onto a vehicle or an animal for transport.
to return / to come back; Compound verb expressing the act of returning to a previous location.
to wait / to watch the path / to anticipate; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to wait anxiously or look forward to someone's arrival.
to pray / to bless / to wish well; Compound verb expressing the act of asking God for something or wishing someone well.
to give thanks / to be grateful; Compound verb used to express gratitude to God or to another person.
to have patience / to endure / to wait; Compound verb expressing the act of remaining calm and steadfast during difficult times or while waiting.
to trust / to rely on / to depend; Compound verb expressing the act of having confidence in someone or something.
to believe / to trust / to be sure; Compound verb expressing the act of accepting something as true or having firm conviction.
to doubt / to suspect; Compound verb expressing a lack of certainty or suspicion about someone or something.
to worry / to think / to care / to plan; Compound verb with dual meanings: to be anxious about something or to think/reflect deeply.
to be angry / to get mad; Compound verb expressing the feeling of annoyance, displeasure, or hostility.
to love / to have affection; (Similar to pyār karnā, but often used for deeper or more formal love). To love.
to like / to choose / to prefer; Compound verb expressing the act of finding something agreeable or making a choice.
to dislike; Compound verb expressing the act of not liking something.
to praise / to define / to compliment; Compound verb expressing approval or admiration, or providing a definition of a word.
to backbite / to speak ill / to do evil; Compound verb meaning to speak badly about someone in their absence or to commit a bad deed.
to complain; Compound verb expressing dissatisfaction or annoyance about something to someone else.
to advise / to suggest / to consult; Compound verb expressing the act of providing a recommendation or guidance to someone.
to obey / to follow an order; Compound verb expressing the act of following a command or instruction given by an authority.
to make someone wait; Causative compound verb meaning to cause another person to stay in a place until one arrives or something happens.
to remind; Compound verb meaning to cause someone to remember something they might have forgotten.
to be understood / to make sense; Idiomatic compound verb expressing that something has become clear to the subject.
to find out / to come to know / to discover; Idiomatic compound verb indicating the discovery of information or a fact.
to be of use / to be useful / to be martyred (context dependent); Compound verb meaning to be helpful in a situation, or specifically to die for a cause (in military/heroic contexts).
to occur / to happen / to behave; Compound verb meaning for an event to happen or describing how one conducts oneself toward others.
to be visible / to appear / to be seen; Compound verb indicating that something can be perceived with the eyes.
to be audible / to be heard; Compound verb indicating that a sound is reaching the ears.
to be visible / to appear; Compound verb used to indicate that something is becoming apparent or can be seen.
to be felt / to be perceived / to seem; Compound verb expressing a sensation or a feeling that is perceived by the mind or body.
to find out / to inquire / to ascertain; Compound verb meaning to make an effort to obtain information or to verify a fact.
to research / to investigate / to verify; Compound verb meaning to conduct a detailed study or investigation into a matter.
to ponder / to consider / to meditate; Compound verb meaning to think deeply or carefully about something.
to take care / to look after / to keep in mind; Compound verb meaning to watch over someone/something or to remember a particular fact.
to be careful / to pay attention / to keep in mind; (Similar to dhyān denā, but often refers to continuous awareness or caution). To be careful.
to care / to mind / to be concerned; Compound verb expressing the act of being concerned about something or someone.
to dare / to have courage / to venture; Compound verb expressing the act of showing bravery or resolving to do something difficult.
to compete / to face / to oppose; Compound verb meaning to take part in a contest or to confront a difficult situation/person.
to be hostile / to act as an enemy; Compound verb expressing the act of showing enmity or being in a state of conflict with someone.
to make friends / to befriend; Compound verb expressing the act of establishing a friendly relationship with someone.
to do good / to act virtuously; Compound verb expressing the act of performing a good or righteous deed.
to sin / to commit a transgression; Compound verb expressing the act of violating a religious or moral law.
to make a mistake / to err; Compound verb expressing the act of doing something incorrectly or making a wrong judgment.
to struggle / to strive / to exert effort; Compound verb expressing the act of making a continuous and difficult effort to achieve something.
to cooperate / to collaborate; Compound verb expressing the act of working together with others toward a common goal.
to arrange / to manage / to organize; Compound verb expressing the act of planning or setting up an event, system, or space.
to spend / to consume / to use up; Compound verb meaning to use money, time, or energy for a purpose.
to change / to exchange / to transform; Compound verb expressing the act of making something different or replacing one thing with another.
to take revenge / to retaliate; Compound verb expressing the act of punishing someone who has harmed you.
to reward / to compensate / to pay back; Compound verb expressing the act of giving something in return for a service, favor, or harm.
to do justice / to be fair; Compound verb expressing the act of treating people fairly and according to the law/truth.
to oppress / to act cruelly / to do injustice; Compound verb expressing the act of treating someone with cruelty or taking away their rights.
to steal / to thieve; Compound verb expressing the act of taking something that belongs to someone else without permission.
to kill / to murder; Compound verb expressing the act of ending a life intentionally.
to deceive / to cheat / to betray; Compound verb expressing the act of misleading someone through lies or trickery.
to lie / to tell a lie; Compound verb expressing the act of stating something that one knows is not true.
to speak the truth; Compound verb expressing the act of stating facts as they are.
to break a promise; Compound verb expressing the failure to fulfill a commitment or pledge made earlier.
to keep a promise / to fulfill a pledge; Compound verb expressing the act of successfully fulfilling a commitment.
to respect / to honor / to value; Compound verb expressing the act of showing high regard or esteem for someone.
to humiliate / to insult / to degrade; Compound verb expressing the act of making someone feel ashamed or lower in status.
to be proud / to take pride in; Compound verb expressing a feeling of deep pleasure or satisfaction in one's own or another's achievements.
to be grateful / to acknowledge a favor; Compound verb expressing the act of feeling or showing gratitude for someone's kindness.
to express gratitude / to thank; (Formal version of shukr karnā). Compound verb used to formally thank someone or God.
to apologize / to excuse oneself; Compound verb expressing regret for a mistake or declining an invitation politely.
to ask for forgiveness / to apologize; Compound verb expressing a direct request for forgiveness from someone for a wrong done.
to compensate / to make up for / to redress; Compound verb expressing the act of making amends for a loss, damage, or mistake.
to defame / to slander / to bring a bad name; Compound verb expressing the act of harming someone's reputation through false or malicious talk.
to earn a good name / to build a reputation; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to achieve respect and honor through good deeds.
to gain fame / to become famous; Compound verb expressing the act of becoming widely known to the public.
to use foul language / to be rude / to speak harshly; Compound verb expressing the act of using insulting or disrespectful words.
to bless / to give a prayer / to wish well; Compound verb expressing the act of praying for someone's success or well-being.
to curse / to give a bad prayer / to ill-wish; Compound verb expressing the act of praying for someone's misfortune or ruin.
to advise / to preach / to counsel; Compound verb expressing the act of giving moral guidance or practical advice.
to bequeath / to make a will / to command (final); Compound verb expressing the act of making a formal statement about the distribution of property after death or a final request.
to invite / to host a feast; Compound verb expressing the act of asking someone to attend an event or a meal.
to show hospitality / to host; Compound verb expressing the act of being a good host and taking care of guests.
to join / to participate / to become a member; Formal compound verb meaning to become part of a group, party, or organization.
to participate / to attend / to take part; Compound verb expressing the act of being present and active in an event or meeting.
to oppose / to resist / to contradict; Compound verb expressing the act of being against an idea, person, or policy.
to support / to endorse / to second (a motion); Compound verb expressing the act of supporting an idea or statement made by someone else.
to decide / to judge / to resolve; Compound verb expressing the act of making a choice or reaching a conclusion after consideration.
to intend / to resolve / to make up one's mind; Compound verb expressing the act of planning or resolving to do something.
to plan / to scheme / to devise a strategy; Compound verb expressing the act of making a detailed plan for a future action.
to arrange / to manage / to organize (ceremonial/grand); Compound verb expressing the act of making arrangements, often for a formal or significant event.
to struggle / to run around / to exert great effort; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of working very hard and being constantly busy to achieve a goal.
to hustle / to run around / to be busy with chores; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the physical act of being busy with various tasks or errands.
to work with soul and life / to be extremely dedicated; Compound verb expressing the act of working with extreme dedication and self-sacrifice.

to waste time; Compound verb expressing the act of spending time on useless or unproductive activities.
to be deceived / to be cheated / to be tricked; Passive compound verb used when the subject is the victim of a deception or trick.
to be beaten / to get a thrashing; Passive compound verb used when the subject receives physical blows or punishment.
to be wounded / to receive a cut; (Similar to choṭ lagnā, but usually refers to an open wound or a deep emotional hurt). To be wounded.
to stumble / to trip / to be hit by an obstacle; Compound verb expressing the act of hitting one's foot against something or figuratively failing in a task.
to fall down / to collapse; Compound verb expressing a sudden fall from a height or a physical collapse.
to take support / to rely on / to lean on; Compound verb expressing the act of using something or someone for physical or moral support.
to give support / to help / to sustain; Compound verb expressing the act of providing assistance or physical support to someone in need.
to extend a hand (help) / to reach out; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to offer help or to attempt to reach for something.
to give a shoulder (help) / to be a pallbearer; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to help someone in their burden or specifically to carry a coffin during a funeral.
to carry a funeral / to perform a funeral procession; Compound verb specifically referring to the act of lifting and carrying the deceased toward the burial ground.
to bury / to inter; Compound verb expressing the act of putting a dead body into the ground.

to offer condolences / to sympathize with the bereaved; Compound verb expressing the act of visiting the family of the deceased to offer sympathy and prayers.
to mourn / to lament / to beat the chest (ceremonial); Compound verb expressing the act of mourning for the dead, often involving public or ceremonial displays of grief.
to endure / to suffer through / to weather (a storm); Verb expressing the act of undergoing a long or difficult experience or hardship.
to make someone cry; Causative verb meaning to cause someone else to shed tears or feel extreme sorrow.
to make someone laugh; Causative verb meaning to cause someone else to feel amused and laugh.
to smile; Verb expressing the act of forming a pleased or kind expression on the face.
to burst out laughing / to guffaw; Compound verb expressing a sudden, loud, and hearty laugh.
to make fun of / to mock / to ridicule; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of teasing someone in an unkind or mocking way.
to use sarcasm / to taunt / to mock (intellectually); Compound verb expressing the act of using irony or sharp words to mock or convey contempt.

to speak ill / to malign; Compound verb expressing the act of saying bad things about someone, whether in their presence or absence.
to flatter / to butter up; Compound verb expressing the act of praising someone excessively or insincerely to gain a favor.
to sycophant / to fawn / to be a toady; (Stronger than khushāmad). Compound verb expressing the act of behaving in an excessively submissive way to win favor.
to worship / to serve (God); Compound verb expressing the act of performing religious devotion and service to God.
to prostrate / to bow down; Compound verb expressing the act of touching the ground with the forehead in submission or worship.
to mention / to remember (God) / to state; Compound verb expressing the act of speaking about something or reciting the names/attributes of God.
to recite (Holy Book); Compound verb specifically used for the act of reading or reciting verses from a holy scripture, especially the Quran.
to preach / to deliver a sermon; Compound verb expressing the act of giving a religious or moral discourse to a congregation.
to propagate (faith) / to preach / to spread a message; Compound verb expressing the act of spreading a religious message or an ideology to others.
to give guidance / to direct / to instruct; Compound verb expressing the act of providing spiritual or practical direction to someone.
to mislead / to lead astray; Compound verb expressing the act of making someone lose their way physically or morally.
to lead astray / to entice / to tempt; Verb expressing the act of persuading someone to do something wrong or foolish through trickery or temptation.
to instigate / to entice / to provoke; (Stronger than behkānā). Verb expressing the act of inciting someone to commit a negative act or crime.
to incite / to provoke / to stimulate; Verb expressing the act of encouraging or stirring someone to take an action, often a rebellious or aggressive one.
to reconcile / to make peace / to settle a dispute; Compound verb expressing the act of ending a conflict and reaching an agreement with an opponent.
to persuade / to make someone agree / to please; Compound verb expressing the act of making someone willing to do something or gaining their consent/pleasure.
to feel shy / to be ashamed / to blush; Verb expressing the feeling of shyness, modesty, or shame.
to be worried / to be upset / to be troubled; Compound verb expressing a state of anxiety or being bothered by something.
to find peace / to be at ease / to find tranquility; Compound verb expressing the act of attaining a state of mental or physical calmness.
to provide comfort / to give rest / to soothe; Compound verb meaning to do something that makes another person feel comfortable or relieved of pain/stress.
to give pain / to trouble / to bother; Compound verb meaning to cause physical or mental distress to someone.
to hurt (emotionally) / to cause sorrow; Compound verb specifically referring to hurting someone's feelings or causing them sadness.
to celebrate happiness / to rejoice; Compound verb expressing the act of celebrating or showing joy for an achievement or event.
to celebrate Eid; (Specific cultural verb). Compound verb referring to performing the rituals and festivities of the Eid holiday.
to celebrate birthday; Compound verb referring to celebrating the anniversary of one's birth.
to mourn / to be in mourning; Compound verb expressing the act of showing sorrow for the death of someone, often for a specific period.
to forget / to overlook / to omit; Formal compound verb meaning to fail to remember or to intentionally ignore something.
to ignore / to overlook / to disregard; Compound verb expressing the act of not paying attention to something or someone, either intentionally or unintentionally.
to forgive / to overlook / to pass over; Noble compound verb meaning to ignore someone's mistake and choose not to punish or remember it.
to set aside / to disregard / to keep aside; Compound verb used to indicate that something is being left out of consideration for the moment.
to travel / to journey / to voyage; Compound verb expressing the act of going from one place to another, especially over a long distance.
to depart / to set out / to leave (for a destination); Compound verb expressing the act of starting a journey or leaving for a specific place.
to reach destination / to achieve a goal; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of successfully arriving at one's travel destination or life goal.
to show the way / to guide / to direct; Compound verb meaning to provide physical or moral direction to someone.
to go astray / to lose one's way / to wander; Compound verb expressing the act of losing the correct path physically or ethically.
to get lost / to disappear / to be absorbed in thought; Compound verb expressing the act of becoming lost or being so focused on something that one loses awareness of surroundings.
to search / to look for / to seek; Compound verb expressing the act of trying to find someone or something.
to be available / to be obtainable / to be at hand; Compound verb expressing the state of something being ready for use or easy to reach.
to gain access / to reach / to approach; Formal compound verb meaning to achieve the ability to enter a place or contact a person.
to interfere / to intervene / to interrupt; Compound verb expressing the act of involving oneself in a matter where one is not needed or invited.

to check / to question / to restrain / to hinder; Compound verb expressing the act of constantly questioning or stopping someone from doing something.
to impose a ban / to restrict / to limit; Compound verb expressing the act of legally or formally forbidding an action or item.
to free / to liberate / to release; Compound verb expressing the act of giving freedom to a prisoner, a slave, or a country.
to imprison / to cage / to confine; Compound verb expressing the act of putting someone in jail or confining something in a restricted space.
to arrest / to capture / to seize; Compound verb expressing the act of legally taking someone into custody by the police.
to get released / to gain freedom / to be acquitted; Compound verb expressing the act of being set free from prison or a difficult situation.
to give bail / to guarantee / to stand surety; Compound verb expressing the act of providing a legal or personal guarantee for someone's appearance or behavior.
to testify / to give evidence / to bear witness; Compound verb expressing the act of stating what one has seen or known, especially in a court of law.
to present proof / to provide evidence; Compound verb expressing the act of showing facts or items that confirm the truth of a statement.
to confess / to admit / to affirm / to promise; Compound verb expressing the act of admitting a truth, a crime, or making a formal affirmation.

to prove / to establish / to demonstrate; Compound verb expressing the act of using evidence to show that something is true or exists.
to accuse / to blame / to indict; Compound verb expressing the act of stating that someone is responsible for a crime or a mistake.
to level a slander / to falsely accuse (vivid); (Vivid/Strong version of ilzām lagānā). Compound verb specifically referring to malicious false accusations.
to get acquittal / to be exonerated; Formal compound verb meaning to be declared innocent and free from charges in a court.
to receive punishment / to be sentenced; Compound verb expressing the state of receiving retribution for an offense.
to hang (execution) / to execute by hanging; Compound verb specifically referring to the death penalty carried out by hanging.
to be killed / to be murdered / to be assassinated; Passive compound verb used when the subject is the victim of a murder or homicide.
to be martyred / to die for a cause; (Specific religious/noble term). Compound verb referring to dying in the way of God, for one's country, or a righteous cause.
to be buried / to be interred; Passive compound verb specifically used for the act of a body being placed in a grave.
to dig a grave / to prepare for burial; Compound verb expressing the physical act of digging a hole in the earth for a funeral.

to shroud / to wrap in a funeral cloth; Compound verb expressing the act of wrapping the deceased in the specific unstitched white sheets (shroud).
to give a ritual bath (to the deceased); (Specific religious term). Compound verb referring to the final ritual washing of a dead body before burial.
to offer funeral prayer / to perform the Janaza prayer; Compound verb referring to the specific collective prayer performed for the deceased before burial.

to observe a death anniversary; Compound verb expressing the act of remembering and praying for the deceased on the annual date of their passing.
to be patient and grateful / to accept fate with grace; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of enduring a loss without complaining and remaining thankful to God.
to console / to reassure / to comfort; Compound verb expressing the act of giving hope and comfort to someone in distress or grief.
to sympathize / to show compassion; Compound verb expressing the act of feeling or showing concern and pity for someone else's misfortune.
to share sorrow / to empathize / to help in grief; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of being with someone in their grief to make their burden lighter.
to make a scene / to create a spectacle / to perform; Compound verb expressing the act of behaving in a way that attracts public attention, often in a negative or dramatic way.
to watch a show / to be a spectator / to watch a spectacle; Compound verb expressing the act of watching an event or a dramatic situation without interfering.
to clap / to applaud; Compound verb expressing the act of striking the palms of the hands together to show approval or enjoyment.
to whistle / to jeer (with whistles); Compound verb expressing the act of producing a shrill sound with the lips or a whistle, often used for cheering or mocking.
to make noise / to create a racket / to shout; Compound verb expressing the act of producing loud, confused, or unpleasant sounds.
to riot / to create an uproar / to cause a commotion; Compound verb expressing the act of creating a loud and often violent public disturbance.

to spread discord / to cause sedition / to create mischief; Compound verb expressing the act of spreading lies or ideas that cause division and conflict among people.
to set fire / to ignite / to provoke (figuratively); Compound verb expressing the physical act of starting a fire or figuratively inciting a conflict/passion.
to extinguish fire / to put out a flame / to calm down; Compound verb expressing the act of stopping a fire or figuratively calming down a heated situation/anger.

to take away someone's livelihood / to deprive of bread; Strong idiomatic compound verb meaning to do something that causes someone to lose their job or source of income.
to do labor work / to work for wages / to toil; Compound verb expressing the act of performing hard physical labor to earn a daily living.
to earn and bring back / to provide for family; Compound verb expressing the act of earning money outside and bringing it home for the household.
to run a household / to manage domestic expenses; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of managing the financial and logistical needs of a family.
to take responsibility / to shoulder a duty; Compound verb expressing the act of accepting a task or the welfare of others as one's own duty.
to carry a burden / to bear a load; Compound verb expressing the physical act of carrying weight or figuratively bearing a heavy responsibility.
to take a loan / to borrow money; Compound verb expressing the act of borrowing money with the intention of paying it back.
to pay off a loan / to settle a debt; Compound verb expressing the act of returning borrowed money and becoming debt-free.
to take interest (usury) / to charge interest; Compound verb expressing the act of charging or receiving interest on a loan (often with a negative religious connotation).
to pay interest; Compound verb expressing the act of paying the additional amount charged on a borrowed sum.
to mortgage / to pawn / to pledge; Compound verb expressing the act of giving an item as security for a loan.
to auction / to sell to the highest bidder; Compound verb expressing the act of selling property or items publicly to the person who offers the most money.

to besiege / to beleaguer / to surround (a city/enemy) / to block; Compound verb expressing the act of an army surrounding a fort or a city to prevent anyone from leaving or entering.
to raid / to make a foray / to conduct a search / to strike suddenly; Compound verb expressing the act of police or army suddenly attacking a place to catch criminals or seize property.
to charge / to attack / to storm / to make an assault; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of running forward with great force to attack an enemy position.
to assault / to storm / to invade / to rush upon; Formal compound verb expressing a violent and sudden military invasion or a collective rush against an enemy.
to retreat / to withdraw / to fall back / to be repulsed; Compound verb expressing the state of an army being forced to run back after losing a battle or failing an attack.
to escape / to flee / to run away / to abscond; Compound verb expressing the act of secretly leaving a place (like a prison or a difficult home) to avoid punishment or danger.
to go into hiding / to abscond / to go underground / to disappear; Compound verb expressing the act of hiding one's face and location from the police or the public, often for a long time.

to become a recluse / to go into retirement / to seclude oneself / to live in isolation; Formal compound verb expressing the act of leaving society or public life to live a quiet life alone, often for spiritual or personal reasons.
to abandon / to give up / to leave / to omit / to quit (a habit); Compound verb expressing the act of stopping a bad habit, leaving a place forever, or giving up a claim.
to withdraw / to waive / to renounce / to relinquish (a right/claim); Formal compound verb expressing the act of officially saying you no longer want a post, a property, or a legal right.

to renounce / to forsake / to abandon / to leave (worldly life); Verb (often used in a spiritual or poetic sense) meaning to give up family, wealth, or comfort to follow a path of truth or for a higher goal.
to migrate / to emigrate / to move (for God/refuge); Compound verb specifically used for leaving one's homeland for another place, usually to save one's faith or to escape persecution.
to take up residence / to settle / to dwell / to inhabit; Formal compound verb expressing the act of making a place your permanent home.
to stay / to halt / to reside / to stand up / to establish; Compound verb meaning to stay at a place (hotel, camp) for a few days, or for an event to take place.

to watch the path / to wait expectantly / to look forward to / to await; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of waiting for someone with great longing and keeping one's eyes on the door or the road.
to delay / to procrastinate / to be late / to stall; Compound verb expressing the act of doing something later than planned or being slow in performing a task.
to hurry / to make haste / to rush / to be quick; Compound verb expressing the act of moving or working fast to save time or to finish quickly.
to hasten / to act in a hurry / to precipitate / to be rash; Formal compound verb expressing the act of doing something very quickly, often without thinking properly (rashly).
to spring / to pounce / to rush / to flash (lightning) / to dart; Verb meaning to move suddenly and quickly toward something, like a player catching a ball or lightning flashing in the sky.
to pounce / to snatch / to swoop / to spring upon; Verb meaning to suddenly attack or grab something with force, like an eagle catching a fish or a thief snatching a bag.
to kidnap / to abduct / to hijack / to spirit away; Compound verb expressing the act of taking someone away by force and keeping them prisoner, often for money or political reasons.
to win the game / to surpass / to excel / to outdo / to carry the day; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of winning a competition or proving to be better than everyone else in a task.
to admit defeat / to give up / to surrender / to yield; Compound verb expressing the act of accepting that you cannot win or finish a task and stopping the effort.
to lay down arms / to surrender / to give in / to capitulate; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of an army or a person stopping a fight and handing over their weapons to the enemy.

to be successful / to be honorable / to be acquitted / to come out with flying colors; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to be successful in a difficult trial or task in a way that brings honor to your face (literally: making the face red/bright).
to fail / to be unsuccessful / to fall through / to miscarry; Compound verb expressing the state of not achieving a goal or a plan not working as intended.

to be disappointed / to be unsuccessful / to be hopeless / to be unlucky; Formal compound verb expressing the state of someone whose desires or goals were not fulfilled, leaving them in a state of misery.
to be despondent / to despair / to be hopeless / to lose heart; Compound verb expressing a deep state of sadness where a person believes that nothing good will ever happen.
to hope / to expect / to have faith / to look forward; Compound verb expressing the positive feeling that what you want will happen or that the future will be good.

to trust / to rely (on God) / to surrender to fate / to have absolute faith; Formal compound verb expressing the act of leaving the results of your work to God and being at peace with whatever happens.
to give thanks / to be grateful / to appreciate / to thank God; Compound verb expressing the act of feeling and saying thank you to a person or to God for a favor or a blessing.
to be patient / to endure / to persevere / to restrain oneself; Compound verb expressing the act of staying calm and strong during a difficult time or when someone treats you badly.
to be content / to be satisfied / to live within means / to be frugal; Formal compound verb expressing the act of being happy with the little you have and not desiring more than you need.

to get the divine grace / to be enabled / to get the opportunity (from God) / to succeed; Formal compound verb expressing the state of being given the spiritual power and the chance by God to do a good deed.
to receive benefit / to receive grace / to be blessed / to gain bounty; Poetic and formal compound verb expressing the act of receiving spiritual or physical benefits from a saint, a teacher, or God.
to receive blessing / to prosper / to have abundance / to be sanctified; Compound verb expressing the state of having a blessing in one's wealth, time, or family so that it increases and lasts long.
to be completed / to be finalized / to be perfected / to reach fulfillment; Formal compound verb expressing the state of a long process, a building, or a book reaching its final and perfect stage.
to checkmate / to defeat / to outwit / to surpass; Compound verb expressing the act of putting an opponent in a position where they cannot move or win, like in chess or a political argument.
to floor / to dash down / to overthrow / to knock down; Verb meaning to throw someone to the ground with great force, often used in wrestling or in a physical fight.
to crush / to bruise / to suppress / to squash; Verb meaning to press something hard so that its shape is ruined, or figuratively to stop a rebellion or a movement by force.
to pounce / to seize / to throttle / to grab (by the neck); Verb meaning to suddenly grab something or someone with great force, often by the throat or in a way that prevents them from escaping.
to bind / to tighten / to clinch / to clasp firmly; Verb meaning to tie something or someone so tightly that they cannot move even an inch.
to tighten / to brace / to test (on a touchstone) / to stretch; Verb meaning to make a rope or a belt tighter, or figuratively to test the purity of gold or the quality of a person.
to loosen / to relax / to slacken / to soften; Compound verb expressing the act of making a tight knot, a string, or a strict law less tight.
to open / to unlock / to disclose / to reveal (a secret); Formal compound verb meaning to open a door or a heart, or to reveal a truth that was hidden.
to keep hidden / to conceal / to keep secret / to mask; Compound verb expressing the intentional act of not letting anyone see an object or know a piece of information.
to keep a secret / to be confidential / to suppress (information); Compound verb expressing the act of not telling anyone else a piece of information that was shared with you in trust.
to reveal / to disclose / to expose (a secret) / to proclaim; Formal compound verb expressing the act of making a hidden secret or a conspiracy known to the public.

to expose / to unmask / to reveal a fault / to blow someone's cover; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the act of showing the world someone's real, often bad, character by removing the curtain of their lies.
to disgrace / to dishonor / to defame / to humiliate publicly; Compound verb expressing the act of ruining someone's reputation and making them feel ashamed in front of everyone.
to curse / to abuse / to vituperate / to reprove; Verb meaning to say bad words to someone because you are angry, or to wish for bad luck to happen to them.
to curse / to imprecate / to pray for someone's ruin; Compound verb expressing the act of asking God to punish someone or bring disaster upon them.
to bless / to pray for / to give a blessing / to wish well; Compound verb expressing the act of asking God to give someone happiness, health, or success.
to be inflamed / to be enraged / to be provoked / to flare up; Formal compound verb expressing the state of becoming extremely angry and red in the face, as if a fire has been lit inside.

to be furious / to be extremely angry / to seethe with rage / to be a ball of fire; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the highest level of anger where a person loses control and looks like they might explode.
to suppress anger / to swallow one's pride / to restrain oneself / to bottle up rage; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to feel very angry but choosing not to show it and staying quiet instead.
to overlook / to excuse / to forgive / to pass over / to ignore (a fault); Compound verb expressing the act of seeing someone's mistake but deciding not to punish them or mention it.
to bestow / to give / to forgive (sins) / to grant pardon; Compound verb expressing the act of giving a gift or, more commonly, for God to forgive a person's sins on the Day of Judgment.
to sin / to commit a crime / to do wrong / to transgress; Compound verb expressing the act of breaking a religious law or doing something that is morally wrong.

to turn back / to refer / to consult / to return (to God) / to appeal; Formal compound verb meaning to look at a book for information, to contact someone for help, or for a heart to turn back toward God.
to be inclined / to be leaning / to be prone / to be attracted / to be disposed; Compound verb expressing the state of one's mind or heart starting to like something or moving in a certain direction.
to be inclined / to be desirous / to be attracted / to be interested; Formal compound verb expressing a strong desire or a natural attraction toward an idea, a person, or a path of life.
to avoid / to shun / to evade / to abstain / to escape; Formal compound verb expressing the act of staying away from a person, a place, or a bad habit.
to abstain / to avoid / to refrain / to shun; Formal compound verb expressing the act of staying away from something bad, illegal, or harmful for moral or legal reasons.
to abstain / to diet / to take care / to avoid (for health); Compound verb used for staying away from certain foods when sick (dieting) or staying away from bad habits for one's well-being.
to support / to sustain / to endure / to prop up; Verb meaning to give physical support to a wall or a person, or to bear the weight of a difficult time with patience.
to suffer / to endure / to undergo / to weather (a storm); Verb expressing the act of going through a long period of trouble or pain, often used for natural disasters or long illnesses.
to suffer / to pay for (a mistake) / to settle (a matter) / to enjoy (ironically); Verb expressing the act of facing the consequences of one's actions, or finishing a long, tiring task.
to maintain / to carry on / to manage / to get along / to fulfill (a promise); Verb meaning to continue a relationship or a duty until the end, often despite difficulties.
to pass (time) / to live / to spend / to submit / to cause to go by; Verb meaning to spend days, months, or years in a certain way, or to formally present a document to an office.
to pass (time) / to live / to complete / to finish; Compound verb expressing the act of living one's life or finishing a period of time, often used in formal writing.
to stop / to stay / to wait / to be hindered; Verb meaning to not move anymore, to wait for someone at a place, or for a process to be blocked.
to stop / to cease / to be supported / to be steady; Verb specifically used for rain, tears, or a storm stopping, or for a falling building to be propped up.
to pass away / to be postponed / to move / to be avoided (danger); Verb expressing the state of a danger, a headache, or a difficult time finally going away, or an event being moved to a later date.
to amuse / to divert / to entertain / to console; Verb meaning to make a child or a sad person happy by playing with them or showing them something interesting to take their mind off their pain.
to be delighted / to be pleased / to be fascinated / to fall in love; Verb expressing the act of being extremely happy and captivated by someone's beauty, a song, or a beautiful scene.
to covet / to long for / to entice / to tempt / to be greedy; Verb meaning to strongly desire something that belongs to someone else, or to show something to someone to make them want it (entice).
to long / to yearn / to pity / to be deprived of / to desire intensely; Verb meaning to wait for something for a very long time with great pain, or to feel sorry for someone's condition.
to sob / to gasp / to breathe hard / to be in agony; Verb expressing the act of crying quietly with short gasps, or the difficult breathing of someone who is very ill or dying.
to sob violently / to weep bitterly / to wail / to lament; Verb meaning to cry very loudly and with great pain, often used for a child who has lost its mother or a person in extreme grief.
to be agitated / to be restless / to toss about (in pain) / to writhe; Verb expressing the state of a person who cannot stay still because of physical pain, extreme anger, or a stinging feeling.
to be confounded / to be staggered / to be nonplussed / to be flurried; Verb expressing the state of being suddenly confused and not knowing what to say or do when caught in a lie or a surprise.
to be thunderstruck / to be amazed / to be confused / to be speechless; Idiomatic compound verb expressing a state of extreme shock where a person's mouth stays open and they cannot speak.
to startle / to wake up suddenly / to be alert / to jump (in surprise); Verb meaning to suddenly move or wake up because of a noise, a touch, or a sudden thought.
to be struck with terror / to be cowed / to be frightened / to shrink in fear; Compound verb expressing the state of becoming very quiet and still because of extreme fear, like a child being scolded.
to tremble / to quiver / to shake / to vibrate; Verb meaning to shake quickly and repeatedly because of cold, fear, or a loud sound like an earthquake.
to tremble / to shake / to quiver / to shudder; Formal verb expressing a deep shaking of the body or the earth, often used in a poetic or serious context.
to be penitent / to be ashamed / to be sorry / to regret; Formal compound verb expressing the feeling of being very sorry and ashamed after doing something wrong.
to be shy / to be ashamed / to blush / to feel bashful; Verb expressing the feeling of shyness when meeting someone or being ashamed because of a mistake.
to be ashamed / to be put to shame / to feel shy / to be bashful; Verb similar to 'sharmānā', meaning to feel bashful or to be made to feel small in front of others.
to regret / to repent / to rue / to feel remorse; Verb meaning to feel sorry for something you did or did not do in the past, wishing you could change it.
to be penitent / to be ashamed / to be sorry / to feel remorseful; Formal compound verb expressing the feeling of shame and deep regret for one's bad behavior or a mistake.
to make ashamed / to put to shame / to humiliate / to embarrass; Compound verb expressing the act of making someone feel ashamed of themselves by showing their mistakes to others.
to abase / to humiliate / to disgrace / to insult; Compound verb expressing the act of treating someone very badly to take away their respect and honor in the eyes of society.
to be wretched / to be miserable / to be deserted / to be disgraced; Compound verb expressing the state of wandering without respect, help, or a home, often after losing one's honor.
to humiliate / to insult / to debase / to treat with contempt; Formal compound verb meaning to purposely act in a way that destroys another person's self-respect and social status.
to despise / to look down upon / to consider worthless / to disdain; Compound verb expressing the internal feeling that someone or something is small, unimportant, and beneath your level.
to be disgusted / to feel nausea / to loathe / to find repulsive; Idiomatic compound verb expressing a physical feeling of disgust toward something dirty or a very bad behavior.
to be weary / to be tired of / to be bored / to be fed up; Compound verb expressing the state of losing interest in a job or a person because you have been doing it or seeing them for too long.
to be disgusted / to be weary / to be out of humor / to be annoyed; Compound verb expressing a state of deep unhappiness or annoyance with a situation, often wanting to leave it immediately.
to feel weariness / to feel boredom / to be satiated / to feel tedium; Compound verb expressing the internal feeling of not wanting to do anything because life feels repetitive and empty.
to be tired / to be fatigued / to be weary / to be exhausted; Verb meaning to lose all your energy after working hard or walking a long distance.
to be exhausted / to be faint / to be languid / to be weak from fatigue; Verb expressing a state of extreme tiredness where a person can no longer stand or even speak properly.

to be in a bad state / to be distracted / to be miserable / to be out of sorts; Compound verb expressing the state of a person who is suffering so much (from illness or grief) that they do not look like themselves anymore.
to be in a bad state / to be ruined / to be in a wretched condition; Compound verb describing a person or a place that has lost everything and looks very poor, dirty, or broken.
to pant / to puff / to gasp for breath / to be out of breath; Verb meaning to breathe very quickly and loudly after running fast or doing heavy work.
to be vexed / to fret / to grieve / to be drawn (as thread); Verb meaning to feel a quiet, long-lasting pain or anger inside your heart without showing it, or to be stitched (embroidery).
to smolder / to be ignited / to burn without flame / to be provoked; Verb meaning for fire to burn slowly with smoke but no big flames, or figuratively for a war or an anger to start growing quietly.
to blaze / to glow / to burn brightly / to be red hot; Verb meaning to burn with great heat and bright light, like coals in a furnace or the sun in summer.
to twinkle / to glimmer / to shimmer / to glisten; Verb meaning to shine with a moving, soft light, like stars in the sky or the reflection of the moon on water.
to twinkle / to flicker / to burn dimly / to flutter; Verb meaning to shine with a weak light that keeps changing, like a candle about to go out or a very distant star.

to be extinguished / to be quenched / to be slaked / to be depressed; Verb meaning for a fire or light to go out, for thirst to be satisfied, or figuratively for a person to lose their spirit and become sad.
to extinguish / to quench / to explain (a riddle) / to satisfy (thirst); Active verb meaning to put out a fire, to drink water to stop being thirsty, or to give the answer to a difficult riddle.
to be scorched / to be singed / to be parched / to be withered; Verb expressing the state of being slightly burnt on the surface by heat or sun, or for crops to dry up in a heatwave.
to scorch / to singe / to parch / to burn the surface; Active verb meaning to make something burnt or dry using intense heat or fire, often used for the sun's rays.
to melt / to fuse / to be moved (to pity) / to soften; Verb meaning for a solid like ice or metal to turn into liquid because of heat, or figuratively for a hard heart to become kind.
to melt / to fuse / to soften / to touch someone's heart; Active verb meaning to apply heat to turn a solid into liquid, or to say something so sweet or sad that it makes someone else feel pity.
to adorn / to dress / to trick out / to prepare / to beautify; Verb meaning to make something or someone look more beautiful by adding decorations, fixing hair, or dressing up.
to adorn / to decorate / to equip / to furnish / to array; Formal compound verb meaning to decorate a room for a party, to equip an army with weapons, or to dress someone in fine clothes.
to stop / to pull up / to support / to clutch / to grasp firmly; Verb meaning to suddenly catch something that is moving or falling, or to hold someone's hand to give them strength.
to flash / to glitter / to spring / to pounce / to rush forward; Verb meaning for lightning to flash, or for a person/animal to suddenly move forward fast to catch something.
to pounce / to snatch / to snap / to fly at / to swoop down; Verb expressing the sudden and violent movement of a bird of prey or a robber to take something away.
to seize / to lay hands on / to embezzle / to usurp; Verb meaning to take control of someone else's land, money, or property using unfair or illegal methods.
to collect / to gather in one place / to unify / to bring together; Formal compound verb meaning to bring scattered people or things together so they become one group or one pile.

to pile up / to knock down / to kill / to floor someone; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to make a large pile of something, or figuratively to defeat or kill an opponent instantly so they fall like a pile of dirt.
to be dispersed / to be scattered / to be diffused / to be distracted; Formal compound verb expressing the state of a crowd, a smell, or a person's thoughts going in many different directions.
to scatter / to disperse / to shatter / to throw into confusion; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to forcefully make a group of people or objects fly in different directions, leaving them in a mess.
to root up / to eradicate / to pluck out / to demolish; Verb meaning to pull a plant or a nail out of the ground or a wall, or figuratively to destroy a whole system or a government.
to uproot / to exterminate / to destroy completely / to wipe out; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the total destruction of an evil habit, a disease, or an enemy so that they can never grow back.
to uproot / to eradicate / to destroy / to strike at the root; Formal compound verb meaning to completely destroy something by attacking its very source or foundation so it cannot exist anymore.
to eradicate / to exterminate / to extirpate / to annihilate; Formal compound verb expressing the total destruction of an enemy or an evil force, leaving no trace behind.

to destroy root and branch / to annihilate / to wipe out completely; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the ultimate level of destruction where every single part of a thing (the root and the foundation) is turned into nothing.
to annihilate / to make non-existent / to destroy / to nullify; Formal compound verb expressing the act of making something that existed before completely vanish from the world of being.
to be non-existent / to be extinct / to be null / to be missing; Formal compound verb expressing the state of something having vanished or died out, like a species or a forgotten language.

to be missing / to be lost / to be non-existent / to be unavailable; Formal compound verb similar to 'maʿdoom', but often used for a specific person or an object that is suddenly not found where it should be.
to be hidden / to abscond / to go underground / to be in hiding; Compound verb expressing the act of a criminal or a political leader hiding their face and location from the police or the public.

to be out of sight / to be invisible / to be hidden / to vanish from view; Compound verb expressing the state of something moving so far away or behind something else that the eyes cannot see it anymore.

to be apparent / to be visible / to appear / to emerge / to manifest; Compound verb expressing the act of something suddenly becoming visible, like the sun coming out from clouds or a ghost appearing in a story.
to be manifest / to be apparent / to be clear / to be evident; High formal compound verb meaning for a truth or a secret to become 100% clear and obvious to everyone's understanding.
to grow / to sprout / to develop / to flourish; Formal compound verb meaning for a seed, a child, or an idea to grow and develop slowly into a stronger form.
to grow / to thrive / to flourish / to recover / to be restored; Verb meaning to start growing well again after a period of sickness or weakness, or for a business to start succeeding.

to blossom / to flower / to swell / to be puffed up / to be proud; Verb meaning for a bud to become a flower, for a body part to swell because of injury, or figuratively for a person to become arrogant with pride.
to prosper / to thrive / to flourish / to blossom out; Idiomatic pair of verbs expressing a state of complete success, happiness, and growth in a family or a business.

to be brightened / to be cleaned / to be improved / to be settled; Verb meaning for someone's face to look more beautiful after washing, or for a situation to become clear and better after a period of confusion.
to brighten / to clean / to refine / to improve / to polish; Active verb meaning to work on something (like a skill or a painting) to make it look much better and more professional.
to be adorned / to be equipped / to be decorated / to be ready; Compound verb describing the state of a person or a place that has been made ready with fine clothes, decorations, or tools.
to be adorned / to be decorated / to be dressed up; High formal compound verb, similar to 'ārāsta honā', often used in poetry to describe someone looking extremely elegant and decorated.
to adorn / to decorate / to embellish; High formal active verb meaning to add beauty or value to something by decorating it with ornaments or fine words.
to be cast in a mold / to be formed / to be adapted; Idiomatic compound verb meaning to take a specific shape or character, often used for a child following a teacher's example.
to mold / to cast / to form / to shape someone; Active idiomatic compound verb meaning to give a specific character or shape to something or someone through hard work and training.
to cut / to carve / to clip / to pare / to shave; Verb meaning to remove small pieces from a solid object (like wood, stone, or nails) to give it a better shape or to make it clean.
to turn on a lathe / to polish / to refine / to smooth; Technical verb meaning to shape wood or metal by spinning it on a machine (lathe), or figuratively to make a person more polite and refined.

to rub / to scour / to grate / to abrade / to harass; Verb meaning to move one object against another with force to clean it, to grind it, or figuratively to make someone work very hard as a punishment.
to cause to rub / to wear away / to thrust in / to cram; Active verb meaning to make something rub against another thing until it wears out, or to force an object into a tight space.
to press / to crush / to squeeze / to mash / to rub; Verb meaning to use your fingers or hands to crush something soft (like a flower or a fruit) or to rub your eyes.
to trample / to ruin / to devastate / to violate (rights); Formal compound verb meaning to destroy someone's honor or rights, or to walk over a beautiful place and leave it in ruins.
to squeeze / to tighten / to compress / to clasp tightly; Verb meaning to press something very hard from both sides, like squeezing a wet cloth or hugging someone very tightly.

to drag / to pull along / to trail / to involve (in a case); Verb meaning to pull a heavy object along the ground, or figuratively to force someone to become part of a fight or a court case they don't want.
to stretch / to tighten / to pitch (a tent) / to spread; Verb meaning to pull something (like a rope or a cloth) until it is very straight and tight, or to put up a tent or a wire.
to expand / to widen / to enlarge / to broaden; Formal compound verb meaning to make a room, a road, or your knowledge bigger and wider.
to shrink / to tighten / to contract / to gather / to shrivel; Active verb meaning to pull something inward to make it smaller, like a person pulling their legs in or a tailor gathering cloth.
to shrink / to shrivel / to contract / to be reduced; Verb meaning for an object (like cloth or skin) to become smaller by itself, often because of cold, heat, or age.

to be restless / to toss / to be in agony / to flounce / to be agitated; Verb expressing the quick and restless movement of a person in pain, or a fish out of water, or someone very angry but unable to do anything.
to flutter / to throb / to palpitate / to be in agony / to long for; Verb meaning to move violently with pain or desire, like a wounded bird flapping its wings or a heart beating fast with love/fear.
to tremble / to shake / to quiver / to shiver / to oscillate; Verb meaning to shake quickly because of fear, cold, or a very loud sound like thunder or an earthquake.
to tremble / to quiver / to vibrate / to shudder; Verb meaning to shake with many small, fast movements, like a leaf in the wind or a person's voice when they are crying.

to wave / to undulate / to rock / to slumber / to stagger (with joy); Verb meaning to move slowly from side to side like a tree in a breeze or a person dancing with spiritual happiness or intoxication.

to be jolted / to rock / to toss / to shake / to experience bumps; Idiomatic compound verb expressing the rough movement of a boat in high waves or a car on a broken road, making passengers move violently.
to swing / to oscillate / to dangle / to loll / to rock; Verb meaning to move back and forth or side to side while hanging from something, like a child on a swing or a pendulum in a clock.
to cause to swing / to rock / to swing (active) / to shake; Active verb meaning to move an object or a person (like a baby in a cradle) back and forth to calm them or to play.
to be suspended / to be hanging / to be appended / to be displayed; Formal compound verb describing the state of a picture on a wall, a sign on a door, or a fruit on a branch.
to hang up / to suspend / to post (active) / to display; Formal active compound verb meaning to put a notice, a map, or a decoration in a high place where everyone can see it.

to stick / to adhere / to cling / to be compressed / to be flat; Verb meaning for two surfaces to stay together because of glue, or for a person to stay very close to someone else out of fear or love.
to stick / to paste / to glue / to compress (active) / to slap; Active verb meaning to use glue or tape to join two things together, or informally to give someone a hard slap on the face.
to be joined / to be united / to be set (with jewels) / to be coupled; Verb meaning for two broken parts to become one again, or for a ring to have diamonds fixed into it.
to annex / to attach / to link / to connect / to append; Formal compound verb meaning to join a document to a letter, to link two ideas together, or to annex a small territory to a large country.
to stitch / to cobble / to append / to jot down / to patch; Verb meaning to use a needle and thread to fix a button or a small hole, or figuratively to quickly write down a few notes.
to sew / to stitch / to tailor; Verb meaning to use a needle, thread, or a machine to make clothes or to close a long wound in the skin.
to be undone / to be unraveled / to be stripped / to be frayed; Verb describing the state of stitches coming out of a shirt or a person's skin wound opening up by itself.
to tear / to rend / to split / to lacerate / to burst; Verb meaning to pull a piece of paper or cloth into two or more parts using force, or for a loud sound to tear the air.
to abduct / to kidnap / to carry off / to hijack; Compound verb meaning to take a person away by force or deceit, often to ask for money or for a political reason.
to keep in confinement / to imprison / to detain / to hold back; Formal compound verb meaning to keep a person in a small room or jail where they cannot leave or talk to anyone.
to release / to relinquish / to leave open / to restore property; High formal compound verb meaning to give back land or a building to its owner, or to release someone from a promise/debt.
to withdraw / to relinquish / to renounce / to give up a claim; High formal compound verb meaning to officially say that you do not want your right, your job, or your property anymore.

to vomit / to spit out / to reveal (a secret) / to give back; Verb meaning for the stomach to push food back up, or figuratively to finally tell a secret that you were hiding, or for a thief to give back stolen money.
to swallow / to gulp down / to devour / to embezzle; Verb meaning to move food or drink from your mouth down to your stomach, or figuratively to take someone's money illegally and hide it.

to digest / to embezzle / to tolerate / to stomach (an insult); Compound verb meaning for the body to process food, or figuratively to keep stolen money for yourself without getting caught, or to accept a rude comment without fighting.

to fail / to be unsuccessful / to fall short / to collapse; Verb phrase meaning to not achieve a goal, or to get a bad result in an exam or a project.
to win / to conquer / to gain victory / to overcome; Verb meaning to be the first or the best in a game, a war, or an election, or to get a prize.
to lose / to be defeated / to yield / to forfeit; Verb meaning to not win in a competition or a war, or to be forced to accept the power of an enemy.
to be changed / to be modified / to evolve / to shift; Compound verb meaning for a situation, a person, or an object to become different over time or because of an action.
to fix / to correct / to repair / to cure; Compound verb meaning to make something work again, to remove an error from a text, or to make a sick person healthy.
to get spoiled / to deteriorate / to get angry (suddenly) / to worsen; Verb meaning for a machine to stop working, for a person's character to become bad, or for a situation to become worse.
to build / to construct (formal) / to erect / to establish; Formal compound verb meaning to make a large structure like a house, a bridge, or a road.
to join / to be connected / to be attached / to be set (jewels); Verb meaning for two pieces of something to come together and stay fixed, or for jewels to be fixed into a piece of metal.
to spread (something) / to expand / to circulate / to stretch; Verb meaning to put something over a large area, or to make a news story or a disease known or felt by many people.
to gather / to wrap up / to collect / to finish; Verb meaning to pick up things that are scattered and put them in order, or to finish a long job or a meeting.
to make dirty / to soil / to pollute / to defile; Compound verb phrase meaning to put dirt, mud, or stains on something that was clean.
to dry / to dehydrate / to parch / to wipe dry; Compound verb meaning to remove water or moisture from something, usually by using heat, air, or a towel.
to heat / to warm up / to excite / to inflame; Compound verb meaning to increase the temperature of something, or figuratively to make a person angry or a situation intense.
to cool / to chill / to calm down / to quench (thirst); Compound verb phrase meaning to lower the temperature of something, or figuratively to calm someone's anger or to satisfy a strong desire.
to eat a meal / to dine / to partake of food; Common verb phrase meaning to consume a complete set of food at a specific time of day (breakfast, lunch, or dinner).

to drink / to consume (highly formal/royal) / to partake / to sip; Highly formal and respectful compound verb (Aadaab style) used when offering or describing the act of drinking or eating by a respected person.
to feel hungry / to have an appetite / to crave food; Verb phrase describing the physical sensation of needing food.
to feel thirsty / to be parched / to long for (figurative); Verb phrase describing the physical sensation of needing water or liquid.
to taste / to sample / to savor / to experience; Compound verb phrase meaning to put a small amount of food or drink in your mouth to see what the flavor is like.
to swallow / to gulp / to devour / to suppress (anger); Verb meaning to make food or drink go down your throat, or figuratively to hide or control an emotion like anger or pride.
to digest / to assimilate / to embezzle / to tolerate; Compound verb meaning for the body to break down food, or figuratively to understand new information, or illegally to keep someone else's money.
to be sick / to be ill / to ail / to fall unwell; Compound verb phrase meaning to have an illness or a physical condition that prevents you from feeling healthy.
to feel relief / to get better / to recover / to be comforted; Verb phrase meaning for pain to decrease or for a person to start feeling healthy again after an illness or a tiring day.
to have pain / to ache / to suffer / to hurt; Verb phrase describing the sensation of physical suffering or discomfort in a specific part of the body.

to bandage / to dress a wound / to bind / to hoodwink (figurative); Compound verb meaning to wrap a piece of cloth or a medical strip around an injury, or figuratively ('aankhon par patti bandhna') to refuse to see the truth.

to take a siesta / to nap / to rest after lunch / to snooze; Formal and religious compound verb meaning to take a short nap or rest specifically after the afternoon meal, often practiced for health or tradition.

to be fast asleep / to be lost in sleep (highly poetic/formal) / to dream / to slumber; Highly formal and poetic compound verb phrase describing a state of being completely absorbed and deep in sleep, often used in literature to describe tranquility.
to dream / to envision / to hope / to hallucinate; Compound verb phrase meaning to see images and stories in the mind while sleeping, or figuratively to have a strong wish for the future.
to talk / to converse / to chat / to speak ill (with negative context); Verb phrase meaning to communicate using spoken words with another person or a group.

to be silent / to have lips sealed (highly formal/literary) / to keep quiet / to not speak; Highly formal and literary compound verb describing a state where a person is forced or chooses to remain absolutely silent, as if their lips are sealed with a seal.
to smile / to beam / to smirk / to grin; Verb meaning to make the corners of the mouth turn up to show that you are happy, amused, or being kind.
to make noise / to clamor / to create a ruckus / to protest loudly; Compound verb phrase meaning to produce a lot of loud and unpleasant sounds, usually in a crowd or by a group of children.
to call (someone) / to summon / to hail / to speak up; Compound verb phrase meaning to use your voice to tell someone to come to you or to get their attention from a distance.

to ask for help / to seek assistance / to cry for help / to appeal; Compound verb phrase meaning to tell someone that you need their support or effort to finish a task or to escape a dangerous situation.
to advise / to counsel / to exhort / to admonish; Compound verb meaning to give suggestions to someone about what they should do to improve their character or to avoid a mistake.
to order / to command / to decree / to rule; Compound verb phrase meaning to use your authority to tell someone that they must do something, or for a court to make a legal decision.
to request / to plead / to submit (a plea) / to state humbly; Formal compound verb meaning to ask for something in a polite or humble way, often used in official letters or when talking to superiors.
to confess / to admit / to acknowledge / to promise; Compound verb meaning to say that you have done something wrong, or to accept that a fact is true, or to make a formal promise/declaration.
to tell the truth / to be truthful / to speak honestly / to testify; Verb phrase meaning to say things that are exactly as they happened, without lying or hiding the facts.
to lie / to tell a lie / to deceive (verbally) / to prevaricate; Verb phrase meaning to say something that you know is not true to trick someone or to avoid trouble.
to break a promise / to go back on one's word / to betray / to renege; Compound verb phrase meaning to fail to do what you promised someone earlier.
to trust / to rely on / to have faith / to confide; Compound verb phrase meaning to believe that someone is honest and reliable and will not hurt or trick you.
to be deceived / to be tricked / to be fooled / to be cheated; Compound verb phrase meaning for a person to believe a lie and lose money or trust as a result.
to love / to adore / to cherish / to like very much; Compound verb phrase meaning to have strong feelings of affection and care for a person, or to enjoy an activity very much.
to make friends / to befriend / to fraternize / to form an alliance; Compound verb phrase meaning to start a friendly relationship with someone based on shared interests or mutual trust.
to act as an enemy / to be hostile / to oppose / to bear a grudge; Compound verb phrase meaning to treat someone as an enemy and try to hurt or oppose them because of a previous conflict.

to sacrifice life / to give one's life / to die for a cause / to be devoted; Compound verb phrase meaning to willingly die or undergo extreme suffering for the sake of one's country, religion, or a loved one.
to fight / to quarrel / to battle / to dispute; Compound verb phrase meaning to use physical force or angry words against someone because of a disagreement or a war.
to make peace / to reconcile / to compromise / to settle a dispute; Compound verb phrase meaning to end a fight or a disagreement and start being friendly or cooperative again.

to turn towards God / to repent (highly formal/spiritual) / to return / to seek refuge; Highly formal and spiritual compound verb meaning to turn one's heart sincerely toward the Divine, seeking forgiveness and guidance after going astray.
to worship / to pray / to serve (God) / to adore; Compound verb meaning to perform religious acts and show total devotion to a deity.
to pray / to supplicate / to ask God / to invoke blessings; Compound verb phrase meaning to speak to God to ask for something or to seek help for yourself or others.
to give thanks / to be grateful / to appreciate / to acknowledge a favor; Compound verb phrase meaning to express gratitude for a blessing, a gift, or help received from God or a person.
to be patient / to endure / to persevere / to wait calmly; Compound verb phrase meaning to stay calm and not get angry or lose hope during a difficult or painful time.

to struggle / to run about (highly formal/literary) / to strive hard / to exert effort; Highly formal and literary compound verb meaning to make repeated and energetic efforts, often involving traveling or running between places, to get a job done or solve a problem.
to be successful / to succeed / to prosper / to triumph; Compound verb phrase meaning to achieve a goal, to pass an exam, or to reach a high position in life.
to fail / to be unsuccessful / to fall through / to miscarry; Compound verb phrase meaning to not achieve the result you wanted or expected, or for a plan to stop working.
to lose courage / to give up / to be disheartened / to yield; Compound verb phrase meaning to stop trying because you feel that a situation is too difficult or that you cannot win.

to conquer / to scale (a peak) / to achieve (a difficult task) / to perform (formal); Highly formal and literary compound verb meaning to successfully finish a very difficult mission, to climb a high mountain, or to defeat an enemy fortress.
